title: One artifact, many environments
summary: Build once, promote the same image and the same API definition, and keep what differs in parameters and secrets.

steps.title: Build once, promote
body: Two artifacts travel together from test to production:
1. **The integration image**, built once from one commit, scanned and pushed. Every environment runs **the same
image**. If you rebuild per environment, you tested one thing and deploy another.
2. **The API project**: the gateway's definition of the API (the OpenAPI contract plus the gateway's own settings:
plans, scopes, policies), exported from the publisher or by a CLI such as WSO2's `apictl`. It is imported into
each environment's gateway.
What **differs** per environment lives outside them:
- **Parameters**: backend URLs, timeouts, the gateway endpoint for this environment, which plans are offered.
For the API project, a **parameters file per environment** (`params-test.yaml`, `params-prod.yaml`).
- **Secrets**: backend API keys and passwords, from a vault (Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault) via the pipeline or the
platform, **never** in Git or in the image.

steps.prompt: To save time, the pipeline rebuilds the image in the production stage from the same branch. Why is that a problem?
options: Production may get different code or dependencies than the image that passed testing; promote the tested image instead
Production can't run images built in a pipeline
steps.explain: A branch moves and dependency versions float. Only the exact image you tested is proven.

steps.title: Placeholders
body: In Camel, configuration values are **placeholders** resolved at startup:
```properties
# application.properties (in the image)
catalogue.url={{env:CATALOGUE_URL}}
catalogue.api-key={{env:CATALOGUE_API_KEY}}
camel.component.http.response-timeout={{env:HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS:3000}}
```yaml
- setHeader: { name: X-Api-Key, simple: "{{catalogue.api-key}}" }
- toD: "http:{{catalogue.url}}/api/books/${variable.isbn}?httpMethod=GET"
- `{{name}}` reads a property; `{{env:NAME}}` an environment variable; `{{env:NAME:default}}` with a default.
- A missing value with no default should **fail startup**, loudly. An integration that starts with an empty
backend URL fails on every request instead.
- Placeholders (`{{...}}`, startup) are not Simple (`${...}`, per message).

steps.prompt: A route has `toD: "http:${catalogue.url}/api/books/${variable.isbn}"`. Calls fail with an invalid URL. Why?
options: `${catalogue.url}` is Simple syntax, not a property placeholder; use `{{catalogue.url}}`
steps.explain: Two syntaxes, two moments: `{{...}}` once at startup from configuration, `${...}` per message from the exchange.

steps.prompt: Complete the configuration: backend URL from the environment, timeout defaulting to 3000 ms.

steps.title: Resolve placeholders
prompt: Write `string Resolve(string text, IDictionary<string, string> props, IDictionary<string, string> env)` that replaces every `{{...}}` in `text`:
- `{{name}}` → `props[name]`, and that value is **itself resolved** (it may contain placeholders);
- a missing value with no default → throw `InvalidOperationException` whose message is `"missing configuration: {key}"` (`key` is `env:NAME` or the property name);
- a property that refers to itself, directly or indirectly, must not loop forever: throw `InvalidOperationException` (`"placeholder cycle: {name}"`).
starter: string Resolve(string text, IDictionary<string, string> props, IDictionary<string, string> env)
solution: string Resolve(string text, IDictionary<string, string> props, IDictionary<string, string> env)
string Go(string t, HashSet<string> visiting) => Regex.Replace(t, @"\{\{([^}]+)\}\}", m =>
if (env.TryGetValue(name, out var v)) return v;
if (!props.TryGetValue(key, out var p)) throw new InvalidOperationException($"missing configuration: {key}");
hints: Recurse into a property's value with a set of names being resolved; remove the name again afterwards so repeats aren't mistaken for cycles.
template: Dojo.Eq("env wins over default", "9090", Resolve("{{env:PORT:8080}}", dojoProps, new Dictionary<string, string> { ["PORT"] = "9090" }));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("missing env without default", () => Resolve("{{env:SECRET_KEY}}", dojoProps, dojoEnv));
try { Resolve("{{nope}}", dojoProps, dojoEnv); } catch (InvalidOperationException e) { Dojo.Eq("missing property message", "missing configuration: nope", e.Message); }
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("cycles fail instead of looping", () => Resolve("{{a}}", dojoProps, dojoEnv));
Dojo.Eq("the same property twice is not a cycle", "catalogue.test catalogue.test", Resolve("{{catalogue.host}} {{catalogue.host}}", dojoProps, dojoEnv));
